summary: Full backend + frontend verification of the Home page hero banner image feature. All 5 backend tests pass. Frontend e2e (login → Settings → paste URL → Save → verify hero → Remove → Save → verify default fallback) passes. Hero image on homepage now driven by settings.hero_image with HERO_BG_FALLBACK. Final hero_image restored to the default pexels URL as requested.
action_items: MINOR: Login page emits a React warning 'Cannot update a component (BrowserRouter) while rendering a different component (AdminLogin)'. Likely a setState-in-render inside AdminLogin (probably navigate() called during render). Not blocking, but should be moved into useEffect.

MINOR: A 400 response is logged in the console during the settings-save flow (not from PUT /api/admin/settings which returns 200 and persists). It appears to originate from a secondary call (possibly /api/auth/refresh on cookie-less session). Feature works, but worth investigating to keep the console clean.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py get_settings does `doc.pop('_id', None)` — good, ObjectId not leaked.

SettingsIn.hero_image is Optional[str] with no length cap. A data URL up to ~1.1MB (800KB base64-encoded) will be stored in Mongo. Consider server-side max-length validation to defend against malicious payloads (frontend enforces 800KB but backend does not).

Frontend AdminDashboard sends the entire settings object on save; if a data-URL image is present the request may exceed common proxy limits (Kubernetes ingress default ~1MB). For now this is within limits but should be documented.

AdminDashboard settings-hero-url input value uses `settings.hero_image && !settings.hero_image.startsWith('data:') ? settings.hero_image : ''` — correct: when a data-URL is set via upload, the URL field is intentionally blank to avoid dumping a huge base64 string into the input; nice UX.
Hero.jsx has correct fallback constant and applies inline backgroundImage. LGTM.
startup_event backfills missing hero_image key on existing settings docs — confirmed in DB.
AdminLogin (not in this feature scope) triggers 'setState while rendering' warning; recommend fixing.

If admin login stops working in a future iteration, the admin doc may have password_source='manual' with a forgotten password — reset via a small Mongo script (see this iteration).
